card.title: For Their Own Good
card.instruction: Take charge of another person's choices because you trust your judgment more than theirs. Frame control as care.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I booked you a non-refundable week by the sea instead of the climbing trip.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You love surviving it. I've kept that part.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I would rather lose the deposit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You would pay not to rest? I'll make it two weeks. You're clearly more tired than I thought.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 imposes rest with known deposit cost; A3 interprets enjoyment as survival; A5 diagnoses rejection as needing still more rest.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 climbing pleasure prompts A3 protection; B4 willingness to lose deposit prompts A5 doubled holiday.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 express a real preference and accept a cost to regain agency.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 sacrifice as evidence of impaired judgment, intensifying the same caring control.

specificity.evidence: A1 nonrefundable seaside week and replaced climbing trip establish both cost and overridden preference.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 pay not to rest turns B4 costly refusal into A's reason to prescribe more.
